title: How Websites Talk to Each Other

beats.vo: Hello, champ! Welcome back to Mentr Learn. Are you ready for Chapter four?
beats.caption: Hello, champ! Ready for Chapter 4?

beats.vo: So far, we learned what a computer is, how it thinks in ones and zeros, and the devices that bring information in and out.
beats.caption: Ch 1: Computers · Ch 2: Binary · Ch 3: Devices

beats.vo: Today's lesson is: How Websites Talk to Each Other.
beats.caption: Chapter 4 · How Websites Talk to Each Other

beats.vo: Say it with me… Websites… talk… to each other!
beats.caption: Say with me: Websites talk to each other!

beats.vo: By the end, you will know the secret trip a website takes to reach your screen.
beats.caption: The secret trip of a website

beats.vo: When you open a cartoon on a tablet, where does that cartoon come from?
beats.caption: Where does the cartoon come from?

beats.vo: Is it hiding inside your tablet? Pause and think.
beats.caption: Is it hiding inside your tablet? Think!

beats.vo: Here is the surprise. Most of it is not inside your tablet at all. It comes from another computer, far, far away!
beats.caption: It comes from another computer, far away!

beats.vo: That is the internet. The internet is not one big box. It is millions of computers, all joined together, all over the world.
beats.caption: Internet = millions of computers joined together

beats.vo: Some computers ask for things — like your tablet, phone, or laptop. Let's call them askers.
beats.caption: ASKERS: your tablet, phone, laptop

beats.vo: Other computers answer. They keep websites and videos ready, all day and all night. They are called servers.
beats.caption: ANSWERERS: servers keep websites ready

beats.vo: So the internet is many computers asking and answering, again and again.
beats.caption: Internet = asking and answering

beats.vo: Say it with me: Ask… and answer!
beats.caption: Say: Ask… and answer!

beats.vo: Now, what is a website? A website is like a shop on the internet.
beats.caption: A website is like a shop

beats.vo: Think of your home. It has an address, so a friend or a delivery person can find it.
beats.caption: Your home has an address

beats.vo: Every website also has an address. It is called a URL. You type it at the top of the screen.
beats.caption: A website's address = URL

beats.vo: For example, mentr dot com. The name tells us which shop, and dot com is like the end of the address.
beats.caption: mentr.com → the name + the ending

beats.vo: Say it with me: U… R… L… means website address!
beats.caption: Say: URL = website address

beats.vo: But how does your question travel so far? On roads! Not real roads — invisible ones.
beats.caption: Questions travel on invisible roads

beats.vo: Wi-Fi is a road at home or at school. It comes from a small box called a router.
beats.caption: Wi-Fi: a road from the router

beats.vo: Mobile data is another road. It travels through big towers, so it works even outside your home.
beats.caption: Mobile data: a road through towers

beats.vo: Remember: roads do not make the website. They just carry the question, and the answer.
beats.caption: Roads only CARRY questions and answers

beats.vo: Now let's follow one full trip, step by step.
beats.caption: Follow one trip, step by step

beats.vo: Step one: you type the address, mentr dot com, and press enter.
beats.caption: Step 1: You type the address

beats.vo: Step two: your device sends a message on the road: Please send me this page! This message is called a request.
beats.caption: Step 2: Your device asks — a request

beats.vo: Step three: the server gets the request, and finds the page.
beats.caption: Step 3: The server finds the page

beats.vo: Step four: the server sends the page back, on the road, to your device.
beats.caption: Step 4: The server sends it back

beats.vo: Step five: the page appears on your screen. Ta-da!
beats.caption: Step 5: The page appears!

beats.vo: And guess what? This whole trip usually takes less than one second!
beats.caption: All in less than 1 second!

beats.vo: Game time! Here are three steps, all mixed up.
beats.caption: Game: fix the mixed-up steps

beats.vo: Page appears. Type address. Device asks. Which comes first, second, and third? Think!
beats.caption: Put them in order — think!

beats.vo: First, type the address. Second, your device asks. Third, the page appears. Well done!
beats.caption: Type address → Device asks → Page appears

beats.vo: One more real-life example. When you watch a cartoon online…
beats.caption: Watching a cartoon online

beats.vo: …your tablet does not get the whole cartoon at once. It keeps asking for the next little piece, and the server keeps answering.
beats.caption: Ask for the next piece… answer… again!

beats.vo: If the road is slow, the pieces come late. That is why a video sometimes stops and shows a spinning circle!
beats.caption: Slow road → spinning circle (buffering)

beats.vo: Practice check — the same kind of question you will see in the quiz.
beats.caption: Practice check

beats.vo: When you open a website, what happens first? The page appears, or your device asks for it?
beats.caption: First: page appears, or device asks?

beats.vo: Think: can a server send a page before anyone asks for it?
beats.caption: Hint: can a server answer before you ask?

beats.vo: Right! Your device asks first. Then the page appears.
beats.caption: Answer: your device ASKS first

beats.vo: Let's lock it in. The internet is many computers, asking and answering.
beats.caption: Internet = computers asking & answering

beats.vo: A website is like a shop, and its address is called a URL.
beats.caption: Website = shop · Address = URL

beats.vo: Wi-Fi and mobile data are roads that carry the questions and answers.
beats.caption: Wi-Fi & mobile data = roads

beats.vo: And the trip: type the address, your device asks, the page appears.
beats.caption: Type → Ask → Page appears

beats.vo: Chapter four done! Now you know how websites talk. Superb work, champ!
beats.caption: Chapter 4 complete!

beats.vo: Next, a short quiz to practise. Tap Finish when you are ready. See you there, champ!
beats.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
